newsitem.title: UK: Middle East crude tankers still slow, rates softer.
newsitem.headline: Middle East crude tankers still slow, rates softer.

text.p: The all important Middle East crude tanker market remained demoralised after very slow fixing activity since the start of the week.
Brokers said rates on all routes out of the region dropped off on Wednesday.
Other lifting sectors were busier, with most freight rates broadly unchanged globaly, brokers said.
Rates for Middle East Gulf VLCCs retained a bearish downside seen since Monday, with western voyages only able to command W48 and VLCCs bound for the East at W54.5.
VLCCs en route to Japan were placed at W57.5.
By mid-afternoon, Engen's chartering of the 270,000-tonne Taos to South Africa was the only VLCC business concluded. One other vessel had been reported fixed, brokers said.
Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med rose to W100 from W92.5/95.
"There are few vessels available at the moment, which accounts for the slight rise. By the end of the week, more vessels will be present and rates should settle in the W97.5 region," one broker said.
In the inter-UKC sector rates were consolidating with trendline support at W94, amid increased activity.
There was confirmation this afternoon that Shell's international trading arm Stasco had the 80,000-tonne Hitra on subjects, loading mid-September, travelling to the U.S. Gulf.
Caribbean rates for 70,000 tonners heading upcoast U.S. were steady around W142.5.
